title: Weak equivalences preserve right homotopy classes into fibrant objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. A path object for $Z$ is a factorization $Z\xrightarrow{\iota}P\xrightarrow{(p_0,p_1)}Z\times Z$ of its diagonal with $\iota$ a weak equivalence. A right homotopy from $a:T\to Z$ to $b:T\to Z$ is a map $H:T\to P$ for some such path object with $p_0H=a$ and $p_1H=b$. Write $[T,Z]_r$ for morphisms $T\to Z$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by right homotopies, and $[a]$ for the class of $a$.

Let $u:A\to B$ be a weak equivalence with $A,B$ cofibrant and let $Z$ be fibrant. Precomposition is a bijection
$$u^*:[B,Z]_r\longrightarrow[A,Z]_r,\qquad [b]\longmapsto[b u].$$
Every class is represented by an actual morphism. For any object $T$ and fibrant $Z$, equality $[a]=[b]$ for maps $a,b:T\to Z$ is equivalent to the existence of a single right homotopy from $a$ to $b$.
